annotations.text:
A · Edit on the form

The live patient form IS the editing surface. There is no separate list of questions — you click a question where it sits, a small toolbar appears on it, and its settings fill the right panel.

Follow-ups render inline, indented, exactly where the patient will meet them, tagged "shown when · Other".

Why: the current designer stacks an outline above a preview in one scroller, so you never see the question you are editing next to its effect.

Tradeoff: on a 20-question form you scroll to reorder, and there is no one view of the whole structure.

B · Outline beside the form

A proper tree on the left, the live form pinned on the right. Selecting a row expands it into an editor in place and highlights the same question in the form.

Branches are real children of the tree, on a connector line, tagged "if Other" — the logic is legible without opening anything.

Why: his flu form is long. This is the view that lets him audit and reorder the whole thing at once.

Tradeoff: two representations of the same form, and the patient form is narrower.

Both share the fixes that are not up for debate:

· Follow-ups are arranged BY ANSWER — "when they say Other, ask this" — not buried in the selected question's panel. This is the thing you flagged as confusing.
· A version state in the toolbar: what is live, what is draft, how many unpublished changes.
· The 18-type palette becomes a search field, not a wall of 18 items in a rail.
· Pharmacist-only questions are marked in both the outline and the form.

Both match the app's tokens exactly — Archivo / Public Sans / JetBrains Mono, the purple ramp, 8 and 12px radii.
